drivingQuestion: Whose ruling is followed in the dispute of Beit Shammai and Beit Hillel over which blessing precedes when scented oil is brought — and what conduct disgraces a Torah scholar?
outcomeNote: The halakha follows the decisor Rabban Gamliel (oil first); Rav Pappa's contrary practice is explained away as an evasion. Every difficulty raised on the baraita of six disgraceful things is answered and its clauses are progressively narrowed.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֵבִיאוּ לְפָנָיו שֶׁמֶן וַהֲדַס, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַהֲדַס. וּבֵית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַהֲדַס וְאַחַר כָּךְ מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן. אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: אֲנִי אַכְרִיעַ. שֶׁמֶן — זָכִינוּ לְרֵיחוֹ וְזָכִינוּ לְסִיכָתוֹ, הֲדַס — לְרֵיחוֹ זָכִינוּ לְסִיכָתוֹ לֹא זָכִינוּ. אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמַּכְרִיעַ.
segments.en: «The Sages taught:» If «they brought before him» both scented «oil and» a «myrtle» branch, «Beit Shammai say: One recites a blessing over the oil» first «and over the myrtle» branch «thereafter». «And Beit Hillel say: One recites a blessing over the myrtle» branch first «and over the oil thereafter. Rabban Gamliel said: I will decide» this dispute in favor of the opinion of Beit Shammai, that one should recite a blessing over the oil first, as it is more significant. With regard to «oil; we are privileged» to enjoy «its fragrance and we are privileged» to enjoy it by «anointing» ourselves with «it.» With regard to the «myrtle» branch; «we are privileged» to enjoy «its fragrance, we are not privileged» to enjoy it by «anointing» ourselves with «it. Rabbi Yoḥanan said: The halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «the decisor,» Rabban Gamliel.

segments.he: רַב פָּפָּא אִיקְּלַע לְבֵי רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אִיקָא. אַיְיתוֹ לְקַמַּיְיהוּ שֶׁמֶן וַהֲדַס. שְׁקַל רַב פָּפָּא בָּרֵיךְ אַהֲדַס בְּרֵישָׁא, וַהֲדַר בָּרֵיךְ אַשֶּׁמֶן. אָמַר לֵיהּ: לָא סָבַר לַהּ מָר הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הַמַּכְרִיעַ? אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רָבָא: הֲלָכָה כְּבֵית הִלֵּל. וְלָא הִיא, לְאִשְׁתְּמוֹטֵי נַפְשֵׁיהּ הוּא דַּעֲבַד.
segments.en: The Gemara relates: «Rav Pappa happened» to come «to the house of Rav Huna, son of Rav Ika. They brought before him» both scented «oil and» a «myrtle» branch. «Rav Pappa took and recited a blessing» over the «myrtle branch first and then recited a blessing» over the «oil.» Rav Huna «said to him:» And «does the Master not hold» that «the halakha is in accordance» with the opinion of «the decisor?» If so, you should have recited a blessing over the oil first. Rav Pappa said: «Rava said the following: The halakha is in accordance with» the opinion of «Beit Hillel.» The Gemara comments: «That is not so,» as Rava did not issue that ruling. «Rather, Rav Pappa did» this «in order to extricate himself» from an unpleasant situation and justify his conduct.

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הֵבִיאוּ לִפְנֵיהֶם שֶׁמֶן וְיַיִן, בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: אוֹחֵז הַשֶּׁמֶן בִּימִינוֹ וְאֶת הַיַּיִן בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן וְחוֹזֵר וּמְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן. בֵּית הִלֵּל אוֹמְרִים: אוֹחֵז אֶת הַיַּיִן בִּימִינוֹ וְאֶת הַשֶּׁמֶן בִּשְׂמֹאלוֹ, מְבָרֵךְ עַל הַיַּיִן וְחוֹזֵר וּמְבָרֵךְ עַל הַשֶּׁמֶן, וְטָחוֹ בְּרֹאשׁ הַשַּׁמָּשׁ. וְאִם שַׁמָּשׁ תַּלְמִיד חָכָם הוּא — טָחוֹ בַּכּוֹתֶל, מִפְּנֵי שֶׁגְּנַאי לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם לָצֵאת לַשּׁוּק כְּשֶׁהוּא מְבוּשָּׂם.
segments.en: «Our Sages taught» in a baraita: If «they brought before them» both scented «oil and wine, Beit Shammai say: He grasps the oil in his right» hand, since he recites a blessing over the oil first, «and the wine in his left» hand. «He recites a blessing over the oil and then he recites a blessing over the wine. Beit Hillel say» the opposite: «He grasps the wine in his right» hand «and the oil in his left» hand. «He recites a blessing over the wine and then he recites a blessing over the oil. And» after he has recited a blessing over the oil and anointed his hands with it, «he smears» it «on the head of the servant» so that his hands will not remain perfumed. «And if the servant is a Torah scholar, he smears» the oil «on the wall, as it is unbecoming for a Torah scholar to go out perfumed into the marketplace.»

segments.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שִׁשָּׁה דְּבָרִים גְּנַאי לוֹ לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם: אַל יֵצֵא כְּשֶׁהוּא מְבוּשָּׂם לַשּׁוּק, וְאַל יֵצֵא יְחִידִי בַּלַּיְלָה, וְאַל יֵצֵא בְּמִנְעָלִים הַמְטוּלָּאִים, וְאַל יְסַפֵּר עִם אִשָּׁה בַּשּׁוּק, וְאַל יָסֵב בַּחֲבוּרָה שֶׁל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ, וְאַל יִכָּנֵס בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ. וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים: אַף לֹא יַפְסִיעַ פְּסִיעָה גַּסָּה, וְאַל יְהַלֵּךְ בְּקוֹמָה זְקוּפָה.
segments.en: Tangential to the mention of conduct unbecoming a Torah scholar, «the Sages taught» in a baraita: «Six things are disgraceful for a Torah scholar: He may not go out perfumed into the marketplace; he may not go out» of his house «alone at night; he may not go out» wearing «patched shoes; he may not converse with a woman in the marketplace; he may not recline» and participate in a meal «in the company of ignoramuses; and he may not be the last to enter the study hall. And some say» that «he may not take long strides and he may not walk with an upright posture.»

segments.he: אַל יֵצֵא כְּשֶׁהוּא מְבוּשָּׂם לַשּׁוּק: אָמַר רַבִּי אַבָּא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: בְּמָקוֹם שֶׁחֲשׁוּדִים עַל מִשְׁכַּב זָכוּר. אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּבִגְדוֹ, אֲבָל בְּגוּפוֹ — זֵיעָה מְעַבְּרָא לֵיהּ. אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וּשְׂעָרוֹ כְּבִגְדוֹ דָּמֵי, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ כְּגוּפוֹ דָּמֵי.
segments.en: The Gemara elaborates on the statements of the baraita. «He may not go out perfumed into the marketplace; Rabbi Abba, son of Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said:» This prohibition only applies «in a place where they are suspected of homosexuality.» One who goes out into the marketplace perfumed, will arouse suspicion. «Rav Sheshet said: We only said this with regard to his clothing» that was perfumed, «but with regard to his body,» it is permitted, as «his sweat causes the fragrance to dissipate. Rav Pappa said:» In this regard, «his hair is» considered «like his clothing. And some say: His hair is» considered «like his body.»

segments.he: וְאַל יֵצֵא יְחִידִי בַּלַּיְלָה: מִשּׁוּם חֲשָׁדָא. וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא דְּלָא קְבִיעַ לֵיהּ עִידָּנָא, אֲבָל קְבִיעַ לֵיהּ עִידָּנָא — מִידָּע יְדִיעַ דִּלְעִידָּנֵיהּ קָא אָזֵיל.
segments.en: «He may not go out» of his house «alone at night because of suspicion» of promiscuity. «And» therefore «this was only» prohibited «if he does not have a set time» during the night to study with his teacher, «but» if «he has a set time,» everyone «knows that he is going to» study with his teacher at «his set time,» and they will not be suspicious of him.

segments.he: וְאַל יֵצֵא בְּמִנְעָלִים הַמְטוּלָּאִים: מְסַיַּיע לֵיהּ לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא. דְּאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא: גְּנַאי הוּא לְתַלְמִיד חָכָם שֶׁיֵּצֵא בְּמִנְעָלִים הַמְטוּלָּאִים. אִינִי? וְהָא רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא נָפֵיק! אָמַר מָר זוּטְרָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נַחְמָן: בִּטְלַאי עַל גַּבֵּי טְלַאי. וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּפַנְתָּא, אֲבָל בְּגִילְדָּא — לֵית לַן בַּהּ. וּבְפַנְתָּא לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בְּאוֹרְחָא, אֲבָל בְּבֵיתָא — לֵית לַן בַּהּ. וְלָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא בִּימוֹת הַחַמָּה, אֲבָל בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים — לֵית לַן בַּהּ.
segments.en: «He may not go out» wearing «patched shoes.» This «supports» the statement of «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba, as Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said: It is disgraceful for a Torah scholar to go out» wearing «patched shoes.» The Gemara challenges: «Is that so? Didn’t Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba» himself «go out» wearing patched shoes? «Mar Zutra, son of Rav Naḥman, said:» It is only prohibited when the shoe has «a patch upon a patch. And we only said this with regard to» patches on «the upper» part of the shoe «but» if the patch is «on the sole, this does not» apply. «And with regard to» patches on «the upper» part of the shoe, «we only said this» when he is out «on the road, but in his house, we need not» be concerned. «And we only said this with regard to the summer» when the patches would be visible to all, «but during the rainy season,» when the mud obscures the view of the patches, «we need not» be concerned.

segments.he: וְאַל יְסַפֵּר עִם אִשָּׁה בַּשּׁוּק: אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: וַאֲפִילּוּ הִיא אִשְׁתּוֹ. תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי: אֲפִילּוּ הִיא אִשְׁתּוֹ, וַאֲפִילּוּ הִיא בִּתּוֹ, וַאֲפִילּוּ הִיא אֲחוֹתוֹ — לְפִי שֶׁאֵין הַכֹּל בְּקִיאִין בִּקְרוֹבוֹתָיו.
segments.en: «He may not converse with a woman in the marketplace. Rav Ḥisda said: Even if she is his wife. This was also taught» in a baraita: One may not converse with a woman in the market, «even if she is his wife, even if she is his daughter and even if she is his sister,» for «not everyone is well-versed in» the identity of «his female relatives» and they will suspect that he is talking to women who are not his relatives.

segments.he: וְאַל יָסֵב בַּחֲבוּרָה שֶׁל עַמֵּי הָאָרֶץ: מַאי טַעְמָא? — דִּילְמָא אָתֵי לְאִמְּשׁוֹכֵי בָּתְרַיְיהוּ.
segments.en: «He may not recline» and participate in a meal «in the company of ignoramuses.» The Gemara explains: «What is the reason? Perhaps he will be drawn after them» and emulate them.

segments.he: וְאַל יִכָּנֵס בָּאַחֲרוֹנָה לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָרוּ לֵיהּ ״פּוֹשֵׁעַ״.
segments.en: «He may not be the last to enter the study hall.» The Gemara explains: «Because they» will «call him negligent,» in other words, careless and lazy.

segments.he: וְיֵשׁ אוֹמְרִים, אַף לֹא יַפְסִיעַ פְּסִיעָה גַּסָּה: דְּאָמַר מָר, פְּסִיעָה גַּסָּה נוֹטֶלֶת אֶחָד מֵחֲמֵשׁ מֵאוֹת מִמְּאוֹר עֵינָיו שֶׁל אָדָם. מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ? לַהְדְּרֵיהּ בְּקִדּוּשָׁא דְבֵי שִׁמְשֵׁי.
segments.en: «And some say he may not take long strides, as the Master said: A long stride takes» away «one five-hundredth of a person’s eyesight.» The Gemara asks: «What is his remedy» if he took long strides? The Gemara responds: «He can restore it» by drinking the wine of «kiddush on» Shabbat «eve.»

segments.he: וְאַל יְהַלֵּךְ בְּקוֹמָה זְקוּפָה: דְּאָמַר מָר הַמְהַלֵּךְ בְּקוֹמָה זְקוּפָה אֲפִילּוּ אַרְבַּע אַמּוֹת, כְּאִילּוּ דּוֹחֵק רַגְלֵי שְׁכִינָה, דִּכְתִיב: ״מְלֹא כׇל הָאָרֶץ כְּבוֹדוֹ״.
segments.en: «And he may not walk with an upright posture,» but slightly bowed, «as the Master said: One who walks with an upright posture» and in an arrogant manner, «even four cubits,» it is «as if he is pushing away the feet of the Divine Presence,» as «it is written: “The entire world is full of His glory”» (Isaiah 6:3). One who walks in an arrogant way shows a lack of regard for the glory and honor of God that is surrounding him, and thereby chases God from that place.

moves.summary: brings a baraita on which blessing precedes when scented oil and myrtle are brought, continuing the preceding unit's treatment of the order of blessings
moves.about: brings the baraita on the order of blessings when scented oil and myrtle are brought together

moves.cueHe: בית שמאי אומרים: מברך על השמן
moves.summary: Beit Shammai: the oil is blessed first
moves.about: which blessing is recited first when scented oil and a myrtle branch are brought together

moves.cueHe: ובית הלל אומרים: מברך על ההדס
moves.summary: Beit Hillel: the myrtle is blessed first
moves.about: he decides the oil-and-myrtle dispute for Beit Shammai, since oil yields both fragrance and anointing while myrtle yields fragrance alone

moves.summary: Rabban Gamliel decides for the oil, since it yields both fragrance and anointing
moves.about: the halakha follows the decisor, Rabban Gamliel, so the blessing over oil precedes

moves.cueHe: אמר רבי יוחנן: הלכה כדברי המכריע
moves.summary: R' Yohanan rules that the halakha follows the decisor

moves.cueHe: רב פפא איקלע לבי רב הונא בריה דרב איקא
moves.summary: Rav Pappa, a guest at Rav Huna's, blesses the myrtle first — against the decisor's ruling
moves.about: Rav Pappa in practice blessed the myrtle first and the oil after, against the ruling of the decisor

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: לא סבר לה מר הלכה כדברי המכריע?
moves.summary: the host challenges Rav Pappa's conduct against R' Yohanan's ruling
moves.about: why Rav Pappa did not follow R' Yohanan's ruling that the halakha follows the decisor

moves.cueHe: אמר ליה: הכי אמר רבא: הלכה כבית הלל
moves.summary: Rav Pappa answers that Rava ruled the halakha follows Beit Hillel
moves.about: answering the challenge to his conduct by invoking Rava's ruling that the halakha follows Beit Hillel

moves.summary: the Gemara denies the attribution: Rava said no such thing, and Rav Pappa spoke only to extricate himself
moves.about: the Gemara denies that Rava ever issued the ruling Rav Pappa attributed to him

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן: הביאו לפניהם שמן ויין
moves.summary: a second baraita: the same dispute where oil is brought with wine, ending with the rule about smearing the oil and the disgrace of a perfumed scholar
moves.about: brings the baraita on the order of blessings when scented oil and wine are brought together

moves.cueHe: תנו רבנן: ששה דברים גנאי לו לתלמיד חכם
moves.summary: prompted by the closing clause, a baraita listing six disgraceful practices, with two more in the name of יש אומרים
moves.about: brings the baraita listing six things disgraceful for a Torah scholar, prompted by the previous baraita's closing clause

moves.actor: ר׳ אבא בריה דר׳ חייא בר אבא
moves.summary: in R' Yohanan's name: the perfume ban applies only where men are suspected of homosexuality
moves.about: transmits R' Yohanan's limitation of the ban on going out perfumed

moves.cueHe: אמר רב ששת: לא אמרן אלא בבגדו
moves.summary: only perfume on the garment is banned; on the body sweat dissipates it
moves.about: the ban was stated only for perfume on the scholar's garment, not on his body, where sweat dissipates it

moves.cueHe: אמר רב פפא: ושערו כבגדו דמי
moves.summary: hair counts as garment — and in a second version, as body
moves.about: whether perfume on the scholar's hair falls under Rav Sheshet's garment rule or his body rule

moves.summary: the night-time ban is because of suspicion of promiscuity
moves.about: the ban on a scholar going out alone at night is because of suspicion of promiscuity

moves.cueHe: ולא אמרן אלא דלא קביע ליה עידנא
moves.summary: it applies only to a scholar with no fixed nightly study time
moves.about: the night-time ban applies only to a scholar with no fixed study time, since a fixed time is publicly known

moves.summary: the patched-shoe clause supports R' Hiyya bar Abba's dictum
moves.about: adduces R' Hiyya bar Abba's dictum that it is disgraceful for a Torah scholar to go out in patched shoes
